subject: Human Evolution
title: Extracting Ancient DNA
description: A short lesson to help you apply Extracting Ancient DNA.

hook.text: DNA degrades after death. Extracting readable sequences from a 50,000-year-old bone is molecular archaeology.

buildup.text: Bones from cold, dry environments preserve DNA best. Tropical sites destroy it in centuries.

discovery.text: Clean rooms, contamination protocols, and amplification techniques let scientists read fragments as short as 30 bases.

twist.text: The biggest enemy isn't age—it's contamination from modern human DNA shed by archaeologists handling the bones.

climax.text: Ancient DNA extraction turned paleontology from shape-based science into a genetic science.

punchline.text: Dead bones still have stories to tell in code.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge in extracting ancient DNA?
options: Bones are too hard to drill
